archetypes.pitch: Your creatures do their best work standing still. Tapping them crews the Spacecraft that actually win the game, and Sunstar Chaplain turns each tap into value while Dawnsire, Sunstar Dreadnought pays you for a board full of exhausted bodies. Pick this if you like assembling a fleet and launching it all at once.
archetypes.rationale: Six 'two or more tapped creatures' payoffs sit in W and R, but the 22 Spacecraft they station are spread W5/C5/U4/B4/R4/G4 - any color can supply the ships, only WR pays you for tapping.

archetypes.pitch: An army that gets a little bigger every turn until blocking it stops being an option. Terrasymbiosis turns those counters into cards, Loading Zone doubles them, and Ouroboroid snowballs out of every combat. For players who prefer a board that compounds over a single big swing.
archetypes.rationale: Terrasymbiosis converts counters to cards, Loading Zone doubles them, Ouroboroid snowballs every combat; Atmospheric Greenhouse puts a counter on each creature and then stations into an 8/8 flier.

archetypes.pitch: Nothing you control is precious here; everything is ammunition. Each death switches on the Void payoffs, so Sothera, the Supervoid and Susurian Voidborn drain, remove and draw off the same sacrifice. Pick this if you want a deck where the opponent can never trade profitably.
archetypes.rationale: The 31-card Sacrifice cluster merges with the Void suite ('if a nonland permanent left the battlefield this turn'); every fodder death switches on removal, draw and drain in the same turn.

archetypes.pitch: A patient deck that keeps its threats one step outside of time. Warping a spell turns Void on for free, so Alpharael, Stonechosen and Chorale of the Void punish the board without you ever giving anything up. For players who enjoy holding answers and winning on their own schedule.
archetypes.rationale: Void reads 'if a nonland permanent left the battlefield this turn OR A SPELL WAS WARPED THIS TURN' - blue is the deepest warp color (8) and black holds 11 of 14 Void payoffs, so warping turns Void on for free without sacrificing anything.

archetypes.pitch: One creature is never the plan; twenty of them is. Exalted Sunborn doubles everything you make and Moonlit Meditation copies the board outright, until Devastating Onslaught turns the swarm into lethal. Pick this if you love the turn where a pile of small bodies suddenly ends the game.
archetypes.rationale: 38 token producers under two multipliers (Exalted Sunborn doubles, Moonlit Meditation copies); Pinnacle Starcage exiles the small board then pays 2/2 Robots for every card it took.

archetypes.pitch: Every land you drop is a trigger, and Landers let you drop one whenever you feel like it. Famished Worldsire and Icetill Explorer keep the extra drops coming while Glacier Godmaw makes the whole team lethal out of nowhere. For players who want their mana to double as their engine.
archetypes.rationale: 15 Lander sources convert any color's fodder into landfall triggers; ten typed duals feed the 'differently named lands' payoffs and Icetill Explorer adds a second land drop plus lands from the graveyard.

archetypes.pitch: Your graveyard is a second hand, and the biggest thing in it is always one card away. Xu-Ifit, Osteoharmonist reanimates with no mana-value cap, so Bygone Colossus arrives far ahead of schedule and Singularity Rupture wraths the board while refilling the yard. Pick this if you would rather mill a monster than cast it.
archetypes.rationale: Eight recursion effects backed by a deep mill/surveil suite; Bygone Colossus is a 9/9 that loses nothing to Xu-Ifit's 'has no abilities' clause, and Singularity Rupture wraths then mills half a library into range.

archetypes.pitch: Cast two spells in a turn and the deck pays you every single time. Weftwalking makes the first one free, so Cosmogrand Zenith and Sunstar Lightsmith fire on schedule instead of on hope. For players who like sequencing puzzles where the order of your turn is the whole game.
archetypes.rationale: Five 'whenever you cast your second spell each turn' payoffs plus two cost reducers; Weftwalking makes the first spell of every turn free, so the second one is the one you were casting anyway.

archetypes.pitch: Every creature enters twice and you get paid both times. Warp costs let you deploy early and recast later, while Starfield Vocalist doubles each enter-the-battlefield trigger and Cosmogoyf grows off the pile of exiled cards. Pick this if you like a tempo deck that also grinds.
archetypes.rationale: 32 warp cards double every ETB and Starfield Vocalist doubles the triggers again; warp is W8/U8/R6/G6/B2 and Blink/ETB is W7/R5/U4, so white is a co-equal warp color rather than a splash.

archetypes.pitch: Gaining life is never the point here; it is the currency. Ragost, Deft Gastronaut turns every spent artifact into Food and drains three at a time, while Haliya, Guided by Light converts incidental lifegain into cards. For players who like to stabilise first and win comfortably later.
archetypes.rationale: Haliya converts incidental gain into cards; Ragost makes every artifact a Food and drains three per sacrifice; Space-Time Anomaly mills an opponent for your (inflated) life total.

archetypes.pitch: Fill your graveyard, then treat it as a resource nobody can interact with. Seedship Broodtender mills and then hauls a creature or Spacecraft back out, and Umbral Collar Zealot sacrifices for free as often as you like. Pick this if you want a grindy deck that simply never runs out of material.
archetypes.rationale: Seedship Broodtender is the literal signpost - 'mill three' then '{3}{B}{G}, Sacrifice this creature: Return target creature or Spacecraft card from your graveyard to the battlefield'; Landers that die to their own ability are free sacrifice fodder that also fixes.

archetypes.pitch: Make tokens that turn into lands, then make every one of those land drops count twice. Starfield Vocalist doubles each Lander and landfall trigger while Biomechan Engineer and Genemorph Imago convert the extra mana into a board. For players who want a ramp deck with a combo-shaped payoff.
archetypes.rationale: Starfield Vocalist ('if a permanent entering the battlefield causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time') doubles every landfall and every Lander ETB; green supplies the Landers, blue the selection and the doubler.

archetypes.pitch: Relentless aggression with a resource engine bolted onto it. Every Kavu that enters exiles a card off the top for Possibility Technician, and Tannuk, Memorial Ensign turns your second land each turn into damage upstairs. Pick this if you want to attack every turn and still never run out of cards.
archetypes.rationale: Possibility Technician exiles the top card off every Kavu ETB, and Tannuk pings plus draws on the second landfall each turn - the red Kavu and the green Landers are cards an RG drafter plays regardless.
archetypes.key_themes: Tribal/Kindred; Landfall; impulse draw; Lander tokens

archetypes.pitch: Skip the middle of the curve and get straight to the payoff. The Eternity Elevator and a pile of Landers assemble seven or more mana, Sledge-Class Seedship cheats the payload in early, and Uthros, Titanic Godcore waits at the very top. For players who want turn five to end the conversation.
archetypes.rationale: Three mana engines plus rocks and Landers power out 7-9 mana payloads; Sledge-Class Seedship and Terminal Velocity cheat them in early, and Uthros, Titanic Godcore is the blue top end that the old G-only label hid.

archetypes.pitch: One creature, wearing everything you own. Hylderblade hands out the largest buff in the cube and attaches itself on Void turns, while The Dominion Bracelet gets cheaper to move as its carrier grows. Pick this if you enjoy turning a single small body into a threat nobody can answer.
archetypes.rationale: Nine Equipment plus three aura payoffs with a battlefield tutor; Hylderblade self-attaches on Void turns and The Dominion Bracelet's activation cost shrinks as the carrier grows.

archetypes.pitch: A quiet alternate win condition hiding in the artifact section. Virulent Silencer gives every nontoken artifact creature two poison counters a hit, and cheap evasive Robots like Interceptor Mechan and Steelswarm Operator get to ten faster than anyone expects. For players who like winning on an axis the table forgot about.
archetypes.rationale: One payoff gives two poison counters per nontoken artifact-creature connect, and 22 cheap or evasive nontoken artifact creatures can carry it; the cube's many Robot TOKENS explicitly do not count.

archetypes.pitch: Creatures that look like blockers and hit like threats. Tapestry Warden lets your fat-bottomed bodies deal damage equal to their toughness, and Requiem Monolith turns every hit they absorb into fresh cards. Pick this if you like a defence that quietly becomes an offence.
archetypes.rationale: Tapestry Warden lets toughness-heavy bodies assign damage by toughness and station for it; Requiem Monolith turns damage dealt to them into cards; 30 GUB-castable creatures have toughness greater than power.

archetypes.pitch: Make them throw cards away, then charge them for the privilege. Entropic Battlecruiser takes three life every time an opponent discards and Virus Beetle sets it up the turn it lands. For players who enjoy a narrow, mean angle that attacks the hand instead of the board.
archetypes.rationale: 'Whenever an opponent discards a card, they lose 3 life' off one charge counter, but only two cards in the entire cube force a discard - this is a single-card anchor, not a shell.
